$comment: Second authoring pass for FORM-A. Tightening relevance to student-visible text changed which items the builder selects, so four new items entered the form and needed rationales. Two of them carry weak distractor sets inherited from the source bank; the misconceptions named below are the honest ones those choices actually catch, not invented ones.

q-us45-dok1-1.dokRationale: The student retrieves a three-word label. One recalled fact, which is DOK-1; explaining how a given programme served relief rather than reform would be DOK-2.

A: This is the modern environmental slogan, not a New Deal term. The overlap is the letter R, not the history.
substitutes the modern recycling slogan for the New Deal's Three Rs
B: These words describe repair generally but name none of the New Deal's three aims: immediate relief, economic recovery, and structural reform.
guesses plausible-sounding R words without the programme's actual aims
D: Regulation was a real New Deal activity, but it was one instrument of Reform rather than one of the three headings.
mistakes an instrument of the New Deal for one of its three aims

q-us45-dok2-8.dokRationale: The student must identify what changed in a relationship — the legal standing of workers against employers — rather than recall an event. That is a relationship, which is DOK-2 in intent, though the item is levelled DOK-1 here because the change is directly named in the key.

A: This is the Home Owners' Loan Corporation's work on mortgages. It helped families keep houses; it changed nothing about bargaining at work.
confuses New Deal housing relief with New Deal labour policy
C: This describes why authoritarian movements gained support in Depression-era Europe, not what changed for American workers.
answers with European political conditions rather than U.S. labour law
D: This contrasts two European ideologies and has no bearing on the rights American workers gained under the Wagner Act.
answers a comparative-ideology question that was not asked

q-us57-dok1-3.dokRationale: The student recalls the stated aim of a named doctrine. A single retrieved fact, which is DOK-1; weighing whether containment succeeded would be DOK-3.

A: The Truman Doctrine was directed AGAINST Soviet expansion; an alliance with the Soviet Union is its opposite.
reverses which power the doctrine was aimed at
B: The doctrine ended the possibility of postwar isolationism by committing the United States to intervene abroad in peacetime.
confuses the doctrine with the isolationism it replaced
D: No territory was claimed. Aid to Greece and Turkey was support for existing governments, not colonial acquisition.
confuses supporting a government with acquiring territory

U7-DOK2-0001.dokRationale: The student must characterise a shift in policy direction rather than recall the doctrine's name — connecting a specific commitment to a broader change, which is DOK-2.

B: The doctrine did the reverse: it committed the United States to peacetime intervention abroad and ended the interwar isolationist position.
reverses the direction of the postwar policy shift
C: The Soviet Union had been a wartime ally, and the doctrine marks the point at which that relationship was publicly abandoned.
keeps the wartime alliance the doctrine was written to end
D: The United States remained in the United Nations and used it during the Cold War, including in Korea.
invents a withdrawal that did not happen
